stories.headline: Why this 3-week international break is longest ever (and why that's a good thing)
stories.summary: Fans have grown used to international games interrupting the club season, but this break will be a week longer than before. It's not as bad as it sounds.
stories.body:
It feels like the new club season has only just begun, and yet we are already having to reckon with the prospect of 2026-27's first international break.

While fans have grown used to matches between national teams providing an early interruption just a few weeks into the campaign, there will be something different about the upcoming round of men's international fixtures: It will be a week longer.

While that may sound like a terrifying prospect to many a fan hooked on the top club competitions such as the UEFA Champions League, Premier League and LaLiga, the situation is not as bad as it sounds. That's because this break is the first to fall under FIFA's reconfigured international match calendar.

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

- USMNT's gifted next generation kick-start road to 2030 World Cup

- Messi's emotional Argentina farewell shows he hasn't forgotten criticism

Previously, in the first half of each season there were three separate two-game international breaks held in September, October and November every year, with another the following March. But to minimize disruption to the domestic club schedule across the men's and women's game, FIFA voted unanimously to approve changes to its calendar in 2023. The 2026-27 season will be the first to see these alterations come into effect.

As such, we will now see an extended, 16-day international break taking place between Sept. 21 and Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6) that will allow national teams to fit four matches into one window. This reduces the number of international breaks in the first half of the season from three to two, and limits the total number of weeks that club seasons are put on hold reduced from six to five.

From now on, there will be only three international breaks a season that fall during the domestic campaign. This season, they are as follows:

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

As per FIFA's updated calendar, the fourth and fifth international breaks of the season come in June and July, once the club season is over. That allows room in the itinerary for international tournaments to take place during a period when most club leagues around the world are not active. For example, the finals of the Concacaf Gold Cup, CAF Africa Cup of Nations and UEFA Nations League will all be held next summer. The one exception to this is the AFC Asian Cup, which will take place in Saudi Arabia next year between Jan. 7 and Feb. 5.

While the changes to the international calendar will certainly have an impact when it comes to limiting the disruption to the domestic season, they don't go far enough for Arsène Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development. Speaking in 2021, the former Arsenal manager revealed that he wanted to drastically reduce the current system of five international breaks without reducing the number of games.

Wenger's idea -- which he himself admitted was a "gamble" -- was to stage two breaks (in October and March) or even just one (in October) for a month in total in a bid to reduce workload on players and alleviate the "chaos" and "congestion" in the modern game. All well and good, you might think -- although, were a player to be injured during the month in question, they wouldn't have a chance to play international football again for many months, maybe all year.

FIFA's decision to merge the September and October breaks will be good news for supporters who are tired of having the club season broken up three times in as many months right at the start of the season. However, fans going three entire weeks without seeing their team play is going to take some getting used to.

stories.headline: Chiefs laud Kenneth Walker III's impact through 2-0 start
stories.summary: For a second straight week, offseason acquisition Kenneth Walker III demonstrated how he has helped revitalize the Kansas City offense, tallying 178 all-purpose yards in the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Before Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes walked off the field Sunday night inside Arrowhead Stadium, he made sure to hug one of his newest teammates: running back Kenneth Walker III.

"K9!" Mahomes shouted, referencing Walker's nickname.

After the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts, Mahomes made sure to praise Walker, whose 178 all-purpose yards -- along with Mahomes' 382 passing yards -- demonstrated for a second straight week how the reigning Super Bowl MVP has helped revitalize the Kansas City offense.

The Chiefs were optimistic when they signed Walker that he would add dynamic playmaking to their offense. But he has surpassed expectations, leading all skill-position players in the NFL with 369 all-purpose yards through Kansas City's 2-0 start.

"It's fun for me," Mahomes said of playing next to Walker. "Him running the ball and our offensive line driving off the ball the way they're driving off, it's making the defense have to account for that. If not, we're going to run the ball for 200 yards or whatever we did the week before [against the Denver Broncos].

"You want to be able to do it all. We showcased that we can throw the ball down the field, we can play action and can also still run the ball."

In 30 touches, Walker was able to outlast many of the Colts' defenders as the game progressed. With quickness, elusiveness and power, Walker forced 15 missed tackles against the Colts, which exceeded his career high of 14 from the previous week against the Broncos, according to Next Gen Stats.

"They packed five guys in there [on the line of scrimmage]," coach Andy Reid said of the Colts' defense. "That's a good front, so we knew it was going to be tough, but we had a good mix going, a few screens and a couple play-action [passes]. We ran the ball efficiently enough. [Walker] got over 100 yards, but he had to earn every bit of it."

Walker became the first Chiefs player since running back Larry Johnson in 2005 to generate 175 or more all-purpose yards in consecutive games.

"You can see what the defense is doing and how they're playing," Walker said of his performance improving after halftime. "I get stronger. The way we condition, it's a lot easier in the game.

"We worked on [our endurance] in training camp with a lot of long practices. We knew what we had to do. When you go through those practices, you have no choice [but to succeed]."

Walker's presence was able to impact the Chiefs' offense even when he didn't touch the ball. Mahomes finished Sunday's game with a career-high 14 completions on play-action passes for 137 yards and two touchdowns.

Mahomes even shared that Walker's play was helpful for tight end Travis Kelce, who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown.

"When you run the ball, the play action opens up," Mahomes said. "We built on what we did the week before. Just as much as it's cleaned up the game for me, I think having Kenneth and the way he's running the ball gets [Kelce] into these matchups that he's going to win -- and he showed that."

One reason the Chiefs were intrigued by adding Walker this offseason is because they believed his ability as a pass catcher was an underappreciated skill. In two games, Walker has recorded nine receptions for 79 yards, fourth most on the team.

Mahomes' final pass of the game was a short completion to Walker, a play-action pass the quarterback audibled to on a third-and-1 snap near midfield with less than two minutes left in overtime. Walker caught the pass in the flat and sprinted for a 22-yard gain that put the Chiefs in range for kicker Harrison Butker, who made the winning 40-yard field goal.

"It's super fun," Walker said of playing with Mahomes. "We're able to, I guess, freestyle it. If somebody is open or if the play breaks down, he's able to make a play. It's great to play with him."

stories.headline: Geelong coaching coup as AFL premiership great returns
stories.summary: Geelong favourite son Corey Enright is heading back to where his AFL playing and coaching career began.
stories.body:
Geelong favourite son Corey Enright is heading back to where his AFL playing and coaching career began.

The six-time All-Australian defender will leave St Kilda to work under Cats supremo Chris Scott as an assistant coach for the 2027 season.

Enright was once viewed as a potential successor to Ross Lyon at the Saints, where he spent three seasons as a backline coach and two heading up game plan and strategy.

"I'm incredibly grateful to have worked alongside so many high calibre coaches, players and staff during my five seasons at St Kilda," the 45-year-old said in a statement on Monday.

"While this was a difficult decision, I believe the time is right for my next professional challenge and the opportunity to continue to develop my coaching philosophy."

The 332-gamer and three-time premiership Cat has been billed as a possible senior coach in waiting.

Enright lost out to Josh Fraser for Carlton's senior coaching role and was linked to Melbourne's vacant top job in 2025 before withdrawing from the race.

His name has also been thrown into the mix in North Melbourne's search for a "modern coach" to replace Alastair Clarkson following his sacking with a year to run on his contract.

After retiring in 2016, Enright worked in the Cats' development program and was appointed an assistant coach before leaving for the Saints.

Geelong premiership teammate Andrew Mackie said the Cats were excited to have Enright return to the club and join their experienced coaching group.

"Over the past five years, Corey has continued to develop and broaden his coaching experience across a range of roles," the Geelong football boss said.

"He has a proven ability to build strong relationships, along with an outstanding understanding of the game.

"We look forward to the impact Corey will have on our football program as we turn our attention to 2027."

Geelong have already executed an offseason coup after bowing out with a gallant semifinal loss to Fremantle, with former GWS captain Toby Greene joining the club as an unrestricted free agent.

Rowan Marshall is also seeking a trade, a year after Geelong tried to lure the experienced ruckman out of St Kilda.

stories.headline: Dreyer outduels Messi as San Diego hands Miami 4th straight draw
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.

It was Inter Miami's fourth consecutive draw in MLS play as new manager Kily González oversaw his first league game in charge of the club and cut a frustrated figure after conceding a late goal to drop points.

"We've been here for four days and haven't been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger," González said after the game. "We can't commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn't have happened. It's surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

"We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us."

Dreyer gave San Diego a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute, capitalizing on a through ball from Jeppe Tverskov before deftly chipping over goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Messi answered in the 24th with his 20th league goal of the season. His free kick from the right side went untouched through the penalty area and into the far side of the net, four days after he scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in a 2-0 win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup.

"I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency," González added. "These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn't suffer the way we did in the first half."

The goal was Messi's eighth from a free kick since entering the league in 2023, more than any other player in MLS during that time span.

Luis Suárez put Miami ahead in the 74th minute as Miami looked set to leapfrog New England into second place in the Eastern Conference, but Dreyer scored his second of the night eight minutes later with another fine finish -- this time from a ball over the top of the Herons' backline.

Miami is now in third place with a record of 12-4-10 with 46 points -- 11 behind first-place Nashville.

"But anyway, we have to keep going," González said. "On the positive side, we did some good things, but I need to fine-tune the defensive side because that's what really worries me most."

Earlier Sunday, FIFA announced that the final phase of the 2027 FIFA Women's Champions Cup will be played at Inter Miami's home of Nu Stadium in January. FIFA Chief Football Officer Jill Ellis spoke at halftime about bringing the competition to Miami.

"I think we've seen that this city loves its football. We've seen it this past summer with the World Cup," Ellis said. "I think it's time to bring a major women's tournament here to Miami. I think it's exciting."

Miami returns to MLS play next Sunday on the road against the Columbus Crew, while San Diego is also on the road with a game against Austin FC on Saturday.

ESPN writer Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report, while information from The Associated Press was also used.

stories.headline: Raptors honor Kyle Lowry with golden 'GROAT' statue
stories.summary: Lowry also received a key to the city of Toronto and a special dinner to honor his contribution to the franchise.
stories.body:
With a sea of red, white and black Kyle Lowry jerseys filling the streets of Toronto for an honorary block party, the guard's legacy will forever be stamped in the city's lore with an exclusive commemorative figure.

On Saturday, the Toronto Raptors honored Lowry's career with a block party outside of Scotiabank Arena, unveiling a golden raptor statue. The sculpture features Lowry's No. 7 jersey while dribbling a basketball and stands on a nameplate that reads "The Greatest Raptor of All Time. Kyle Lowry | 2012-2021, 2026."

The statue unveiling follows the franchise's August announcement that it would retire Lowry's jersey number during the upcoming 2026-27 season. It will be raised to the rafters at the conclusion of Toronto's home matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

Along with the statue, the six-time All-Star received a key to the city.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me," Lowry said. "We built something special here -- my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me."

Lowry, who spent nine of his 20 seasons in Toronto, helped bring the Raptors their only NBA championship in the 2019 NBA Finals. He will also join Basketball Hall of Famer Vince Carter as the only Raptors to have their numbers retired -- Carter's was retired in November 2024.

The 40-year-old Lowry announced his retirement in July after signing a one-day contract with Toronto to retire as a member of the franchise.

He averaged 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and six assists in his 20 seasons.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas. What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. Here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Baku, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.

Title leader Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the drivers' championship after picking up his eighth victory of the season at the brand-new Madring last time out.

He leads his teammate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now dropping back in the title race after a retirement in Spain.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 15th race of the season.

- Madring's F1 debut left everyone dissatisfied, even Spanish GP's top 3

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Azerbaijan Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, September 24

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Friday, September 25

Final Practice: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Saturday, September 26

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Sam Walker trains, firms for miracle Roosters comeback
stories.summary: Sam Walker is edging closer to a remarkable comeback for the Sydney Roosters, with Hugo Savala making clear he is ready to slide into whatever role required in the blockbuster NRL preliminary final against the Dolphins.
stories.body:
Sam Walker is edging closer to a remarkable comeback for the Sydney Roosters, with Hugo Savala making clear he is ready to slide into whatever role required in the blockbuster NRL preliminary final against the Dolphins.

Less than three weeks after surgery for syndesmosis suffered in a round-26 loss to the Dolphins, Walker on Monday completed all activities at Roosters training before cameras were ushered away from Allianz Stadium.

The Queensland State of Origin playmaker even skipped and lunged on the ankle with no apparent discomfort.

When speaking after Saturday night's 46-10 win over the Roosters, coach Trent Robinson said he was "pretty confident" Walker would play.

If Walker is fit, it would leave the Roosters with close to their best possible side on the field with only prop Blake Steep out injured.

But it would also leave Robinson with a call to make on Savala, who has filled in admirably at five-eighth for the past two games with Walker out.

Savala, 24, has spent much of this year playing centre, but Billy Smith impressed there against the Sharks.

The other option would be for Savala to be on the six-man bench as injury cover.

"I'll just put my best foot forward, and where that's going to be I'm not too sure just yet," Savala told AAP.

"I am sure Robbo will have a chat with me and a few of the boys.

"If I'm thrown out there (at centre) and that's what Robbo wants for the team, then I am going to go out there and go after it.

"Obviously I love playing in the halves, my preferred position.

"But it is a prelim final so we're going to put our best team out there, whatever Robbo sees fit, and we're going to go all for that."

The humble team man would be happy to just be included in the match-night squad as the Roosters chase a first Grand Final berth since defending the title in 2019.

Despite always being a natural halfback, Savala has cheered the arrival of No.7 Daly Cherry-Evans at the Roosters this year, taking it as a chance to learn from the star veteran.

"You get a different view of the game playing different positions. Centre was good fun this year, playing that position," Savala said.

"Robbo tested me in preseason at a couple of different positions. I trained a bit there and got some reps in, so when I was there I didn't feel out of my depth."

Walker returning against the Dolphins four weeks after sustaining such a serious injury in a Kulikefu Finefeuiaki tackle would be a miraculous comeback.

It would also be a huge boost after the Roosters snapped a four-game losing streak with their 46-10 win over the Sharks.

"We still felt we played some good footy the week before against Penrith. We just put it all together against the Sharks," Savala said ahead of Tuesday's team naming.

"We got the result we were looking for, but we're not going to rest on our laurels."

stories.headline: Brewers savor franchise-record 98th victory as playoffs loom
stories.summary: Milwaukee broke the single-season wins mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering Baltimore 3-0 to improve to 98-58.
stories.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Milwaukee Brewers haven't won more than five games in a row all year. It hasn't stopped them from setting a single-season franchise record for victories.

Milwaukee broke the mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 to improve to 98-58.

"We haven't had these streaks of greatness," manager Pat Murphy said. "We haven't put it all together."

Even without rattling off an extended run, the Brewers have the best record in the majors. They've already clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title and will make their eighth postseason appearance in nine years. Twice in that span they've advanced to the NL Championship Series, including last year, but they have not reached the World Series since 1982.

Milwaukee completed its ninth series sweep of the season while receiving help from all over the roster. The Brewers stole four bases, got a stellar diving catch from center fielder Garrett Mitchell in the seventh inning and had seven pitchers combine on a four-hit shutout for the record-setting victory with six games left.

"It means a lot," said pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.86 ERA), who gave up a hit and struck out four in three innings in an abbreviated start designed to manage his workload.

"It's always a big deal to set a new record, a franchise record at that. Hopefully, we get a few more and get to a little bigger number."

Milwaukee enters the final week of the season two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the NL and needs only one more victory or an Atlanta loss to lock up a bye into the division series.

"It's hard to be in this spot to begin with, and I don't think it's appreciated enough," Murphy said. "I think people don't realize how hard it is for any of the 30 teams to put themselves in this position, and that's what makes me proud of these guys. We're not the oldest team, we're not the most experienced, we're not the most talented. We're not the most a lot of things, but for sure they've proven they're a team."

stories.headline: Colts' Shane Steichen defends OT playcalling in loss to Chiefs
stories.summary: Colts coach Shane Steichen defended his late-game strategy and playcalling in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs, saying he would have gone for the win on fourth-and-8 had Kansas City showed a favorable defensive coverage.
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen defended his late-game strategy and playcalling in Indianapolis' 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night, saying he ultimately was going for the win.

With 4:50 left in overtime, quarterback Daniel Jones connected on a 50-yard strike to receiver Laquon Treadwell, giving the Colts a first-and-10 at the Kansas City 17-yard line.

Trailing 30-27, Steichen then dialed up back-to-back runs for Jonathan Taylor, who collectively lost 3 yards.

Steichen defended the decision and said it was not an attempt to be conservative.

"I was trying to finish the game with [Taylor] with the ball in his hands," Steichen said.

That left the Colts facing a third-and-13 that the Chiefs defended well. Jones dropped back but was flushed from the pocket, running for 5 yards before safety Jaden Hicks pushed him out of bounds.

Steichen said he was prepared to go for it on the ensuing fourth-and-8 had the Chiefs showed a favorable defensive coverage for the Colts' playcall. A touchdown would have won the game under the NFL's current overtime format.

"We wanted it to be the last possession," Steichen said.

Steichen called timeout, during which he said he told Jones, "If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look ... let's kick the field goal here."

Kicking a tying field goal presented its own set of challenges, as it meant putting the defense back on the field. The Colts have given up a staggering 1,029 yards in their first two games and struggled against the Chiefs, something that was compounded by starting cornerback Charvarius Ward (groin) having left the game and All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner playing through a rib injury.

Ultimately, the Chiefs showed a coverage that was not conducive to the play's success and the Colts took a delay of game penalty and settled for a field goal. Kansas City subsequently drove down the field and won on a 40-yard Harrison Butker field goal as time expired.

Steichen also addressed his decision to defer after the Colts won the overtime coin toss. He said he preferred having the advantage of knowing what his team needed to do after a Kansas City possession.

"If we go first ... [Patrick] Mahomes gets four downs going the other way," Steichen said. "It could go either way in those situations."

stories.headline: Why Ashcroft 'narrative' sells Lions brothers short
stories.summary: Levi Ashcroft is testing his theory of "you never get bored of winning" as he hunts a fifth-straight premiership that doesn't even do his success justice.
stories.body:
Levi Ashcroft is testing his theory of "you never get bored of winning" as he hunts a fifth-straight premiership that doesn't even do his success justice.

The 19-year-old will chase a second AFL flag in as many seasons when the Brisbane Lions face Fremantle in Saturday's decider.

Brother Will is pursuing a third-straight title and, fresh off a starring role in Saturday's classic preliminary defeat of Hawthorn, can become the first player to win three consecutive Norm Smith Medals if he lights up the MCG again.

Their father Marcus was central to the Lions' three-peat between 2001-03 and Levi admits it would be the "icing on the cake" to help this Lions side replicate that feat.

But Levi's trophy cabinet is already bursting, given he won three-straight Talent League titles with Sandringham before he was drafted.

There were two Associated Public Schools premierships with Brighton too, including as co-captain in 2024.

"You can never get bored of winning," Ashcroft smiled on Monday after recounting a Hawthorn victory he described as "the most insane game he's played, by a mile".

"I just love winning. It's what everyone wants to do, and especially with these guys. It's a special place.

"And I've thought about that, that some guys play 15, 20 years and don't win one or even involved in one. So I'm extremely grateful."

Ashcroft is preparing to play an even greater role if midfield star Lachie Neale's one-match ban for striking Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan is upheld.

"It'll be disappointing if he doesn't play; he's a huge part of the team and in some great form," he said.

"I'm banking on him being there.

"But we have a good midfield that surrounds him and if it goes that way we're ready to go."

The father-son pick and his older brother have slotted straight into a stacked Lions squad, having grown up shadowing their father when he was the football manager of the fledgling Gold Coast AFL club.

"It's the narrative, that we were born to play in these moments," Ashcroft said.

"But it's all the hard work we've done behind the scenes, to feel ready and prepared for these moments, to really attack them and make an impact.

"Will ... elevates himself when those big moments come."

The Ashcrofts are among many young Lions blessed with immediate success.

Ty Gallop is preparing for his second Grand Final in just his 27th AFL game; 70-gamer Logan Morris could win his third title on Saturday, while 17 of Darcy Wilmot's 107 AFL games have been finals.

"It can be about timing and luck, when your career comes and goes," veteran Lions defender Darcy Gardiner, in his 13th season at the club, said.

"So they've come at a good time, but they're playing a huge part in us winning, not just getting by. They're key players."

Levi loved watching footage of his father's games as a kid, but said there had never been great discussions about his achievements.

"He just encouraged us to play and enjoy it and now it's come to this moment and the chance to win three and join him in history," he said.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 38
Goals: 34
Assists: 15

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: UFC 331 results: Van dominates Pantoja to retain men's flyweight title
stories.summary: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan earned big wins on a contender for fight card of the year. Here are the UFC 331 highlights.
stories.body:
If there were any doubts about Joshua Van's championship mettle, they were put to bed after his dominant victory over Alexandre Pantoja in the UFC 331 main event at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday night.

Van outstruck Pantoja and successfully defended double-digit takedown attempts and even dropped Pantoja in Round 5 en route to a unanimous decision win to retain the UFC men's flyweight title over the former champion.

Pantoja put up a good fight, as he held his own on the feet and racked up nearly 10 minutes of control time. His best showings were in Rounds 1 and 4, when he got a hold of Van and successfully took the fight to the mat. But Van did enough to get a win on the judges' scorecards. He has now defended his title twice.

In the co-main event, Arman Tsarukyan earned what could be the biggest win of his career, putting knockout artist Mauricio Ruffy to sleep with an elbow in Round 1. The win likely cements Tsarukyan as the top contender for UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje.

Also on the main card, heavyweight Sean Sharaf pulled off an all-time UFC upset, knocking out top prospect Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds.

Brett Okamoto, Jeff Wagenheim and Dre Waters break down all the action from Los Angeles.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton shuts down asking Ferrari to make changes: 'Never asked for anyone to be replaced'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eight world championship is over.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eighth world championship is over.

Hamilton threw in the title towel at last weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after he retired from the race in Madrid with a brake problem.

His failure to finish leaves him 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings -- the equivalent of more than four victories -- with just nine scheduled rounds left.

A report in Italy claimed Hamilton has challenged Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to make changes to the team's trackside staff.

But in a story posted to his Instagram account on Thursday, the 41-year-old wrote: "I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up on here.

"I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Hamilton sparked hope of challenging Antonelli -- the driver who replaced him at Mercedes -- when he won in Barcelona in June.

However, the British driver has not finished on the podium at the past five rounds and has been openly critical of his team's race tactics.

He also took aim at teammate Charles Leclerc's driving after an opening-lap clash in Monza earlier this month. Hamilton said he led face-to-face talks with the Monegasque to clear the air.

His retirement in Madrid marked his first of the campaign, and when asked to assess his title chances, Hamilton replied: "There's no stopping him [Antonelli] and Mercedes this year. They've done a phenomenal job, and they deserve it [the championship]."

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Nawaqanitawase says NRL return only with Roosters; won't play World Cup
stories.summary: An emotional Mark Nawaqanitawase has ruled out ever playing for any other NRL club than the Sydney Roosters as he eyes the ultimate farewell to rugby league.
stories.body:
An emotional Mark Nawaqanitawase has ruled out ever playing for any other NRL club than the Sydney Roosters as he eyes the ultimate farewell to rugby league.

Returning to rugby at season's end, Nawaqanitawase will remain among the hottest free agents in either code whenever he comes off contract as he routinely floats between the 13 and 15-man game.

But the dual international is adamant he will only ever consider donning the Tricolours after detailing how much of a wrench it is to be leaving the Roosters after a spectacular two-year stint in the NRL.

"If I was to ever come back, it'd only be for the Roosters," Nawaqanitawase, who is of Fijian and Italian heritage, said on Monday.

"It's been above and beyond what I thought it would go like, so I'm enjoying it every week and hopefully I can continue to enjoy it for the next two.

"It's been the best decision ever."

Whether it's scoring the most freakish of tries or setting them up, the superstar winger has proven a one-man highlights reel for the Roosters and almost choked up when talking about moving on.

"It's a bit sad sometimes, like just thinking about leaving everyone," he said.

"But I'm just trying to enjoy it while I can. I don't try to get too caught up in it. Obviously I definitely do reminisce on some of the good times and feel that, but for the most part just enjoy it every day I can."

Headed for the Saitama Wild Knights in Japan's League One competition, Nawaqanitawase also shut down talk of potentially playing at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup.

The happily single 26-year-old will be living alone for the first time and says learning to adapt to domestic duties is a priority.

"I'm just having a bit of time off before I leave the country, spending time with my family, my friends and then having that respect just to start up a new club and find my feet there," Nawaqanitawase said.

"It'll be my first time living out of home, so I just get my head around cooking for myself, working out how things work around the house.

"I'm not that bad but I actually know nothing about just getting an idea of how it is to live by myself.

"So that's going to take a few weeks and if I'm good if I'm going in and out, it could disrupt things."

From Olympic Games and State of Origin to Tests for the Wallabies and Kangaroos, the code-hopping ace has already played on the grandest stages in league and union, but reckons featuring in an NRL grand final would match anything he's ever done.

"It'd be great, obviously," he said ahead of Friday night's preliminary final against the Dolphins in Brisbane.

"I'd say it'd have to be up there with one of those big events: a World Cup, Origin, so I want to do everything I can this week to get there."
